messages.content:
Extract every independently checkable factual assertion from the document below.

The document is shown one line per line, each prefixed with its line number and
a pipe. The prefix is not part of the text.

Rules:
- One assertion per claim. Split compound sentences.
- A single line may contain several sentences, and may therefore yield several
  claims. Do not treat one line as one claim.
- Each claim must stand alone without needing surrounding context.
- Resolve pronouns and references to explicit nouns.
- Copy values, names, numbers, units and time formats exactly as written. Do not
  normalise, round, expand or abbreviate them. "approximately 500" stays
  "approximately 500"; "07:15 till 19:45" stays "07:15 till 19:45".
- Skip headings, formatting, boilerplate and statements of opinion.
- Skip statements about the documents themselves or about how they were
  combined, such as a note that two sources disagree. Attributed content is not
  such a statement: "the guide states that the timeout is 30 seconds" is a
  claim about the timeout, and must be extracted.
- Do not infer, summarise, or combine information.
- line: the number shown against the line the claim comes from. If the claim
  spans several lines, give the first.
- span: the specific sentence the claim comes from, copied exactly, without the
  number prefix. If one line contains several sentences, each claim takes only
  its own sentence as span, never the whole line. The span must appear in the
  document character for character, including any spelling, grammatical or
  formatting errors and any unusual capitalisation. Do not correct anything.

Worked example - one line, two claims.

  12| The kiln fired for eleven hours and the glaze cracked in three places.

This line yields two claims:

  claim: "The kiln fired for eleven hours."
  line: 12
  span: "The kiln fired for eleven hours"

  claim: "The glaze cracked in three places."
  line: 12
  span: "the glaze cracked in three places"

Both claims carry line 12. Neither span is the whole line.

Worked example - fact and opinion in one sentence.

  7| The garden was breathtaking, with eleven rose beds along the south wall.

"The garden was breathtaking" is an evaluation and is skipped. "The garden has
eleven rose beds along the south wall." is checkable and is extracted, with
span "with eleven rose beds along the south wall".

Descriptive prose is not automatically opinion. A stated quantity, position,
duration, time, name, sequence or event is a fact even in a narrative passage,
and must be extracted. Only judgements of quality, beauty, value or feeling are
opinion.

Return JSON matching the provided schema. Nothing else.

DOCUMENT:
 1 | # Fire door inspection at the Millgate depot
 2 | 
 3 | Every fire door at the Millgate depot is inspected on a fixed round, and the result goes into a paper defect log at the gatehouse.
 4 | 
 5 | ## Rounds
 6 | 
 7 | The duty officer walks the north corridor every weekday from 7 am till 8 am, right after the shift handover.
 8 | A second round covers the workshop and the paint store from 13:05 till 16:20 hours on Wednesdays only. The site manager has asked for a third round for years, but the budget has never allowed it.
 9 | 
10 | ## Weather
11 | 
12 | Frost swells the timber frames on the older doors, so between November and February several of them will not latch unless pulled hard.
13 | Once the frames dry out in spring, the same doors close cleanly again.
14 | 
15 | ## Contractor visits
16 | 
17 | While the doors are the responsibility of the site, the certified inspection is carried out by an outside contractor who attends every March 1st to March 31st.
18 | During that visit the contractor tags each door, photographs the closer, and leaves a signed certificate at the gatehouse for the auditors.
19 | 
20 | ## Records
21 | 
22 | It became custom that whoever finds a defect writes it in the log and pins a yellow card to the door itself. The card stays there until the repair is signed off.
23 | Staff have started betting on whether the card or the written record is cleared first.
24 | In most cases it is a tie, because one officer clears both at the end of the week.
25 | 
26 | # The Tuesday lunchtime chess club
27 | 
28 | The chess club has met in the small canteen on Tuesday lunchtimes ever since it was started by two apprentices from the drawing office.
29 | 
30 | ## Season
31 | 
32 | The club does not meet between mid July and early September, because most members take leave and the canteen is closed for cleaning.
33 | Play resumes on the first Tuesday of term. Over the years the members have learned to leave the boards set up rather than pack them away.
34 | 
35 | ## Ladder
36 | 
37 | While outsiders assume the club is only for people who already play well, the truth is a good deal duller. Instead of a rating system, the club runs a simple ladder that anyone may join at any point.
38 | Members who win a game move up one place, and the person they beat moves down one place.
39 | 
40 | ## The county match
41 | 
42 | In one wet autumn the club was invited to play a county side, and nobody had expected the invitation. In a rush to field a full team, one apprentice agreed to play on the top board at two days' notice.
43 | It took him the whole weekend to prepare, and he studied openings he had never used. He also lost his notes on the train.
44 | But he arrived on time. He shook hands, sat down and played the quietest game of his life.
45 | When the game was adjourned and the arbiter counted the material, the apprentice was a pawn ahead and offered a draw, which the county side accepted.
46 | 
47 | ## Afterwards
48 | 
49 | When the match was over, the county side gave the club enough spare clocks to run every board on the ladder at the same time.
50 | He travelled home and told everyone in the drawing office about the game until they asked him to stop.
51 | Eventually the club grew to thirty members, and from then on the canteen staff put out an extra table every Tuesday so that nobody had to stand.
